body: Use quality metrics (ROCE/ROIC, cash conversion, leverage) to decide *whether* to own a business. Use valuation metrics (FCF yield, EV/EBITDA, PEG, reverse DCF) to decide *at what price*. The most robust valuation discipline for a retail investor is the **reverse DCF**: ask what growth the price implies, then judge whether that is plausible.

`person:group-burman-dabur` · flag: **clean (Dabur); mostly-clean (Religare/Eveready takeovers)** · confidence: verified · tickers: DABUR, EVEREADY, RELIGARE

Flag: CLEAN (Dabur) / MOSTLY-CLEAN (family-office takeovers). Dabur India is professionally managed (family separated ownership from management in 1998), with no promoter pledging, consistent dividends and no regulator findings of diversion. The Burmans deploy family capital via Puran Associates/VIC Enterprises etc. into turnarounds: Eveready Industries (creeping acquisition and open offer in 2022 after the Khaitan group's lenders sold shares) and Religare Enterprises. Religare: after open-market purchases (Sep-2023, +5.27% on a 21.54% base) triggered an open offer for 26% at Rs 235/share (~Rs 2,116 cr), a prolonged fight followed with chairperson Rashmi Saluja (who opposed the offer; independent directors called the price low) and a counter-offer at Rs 275 by US investor Digvijay (Danny) Gaekwad that SEBI rejected; the open offer finally ran 27-Jan to 7-Feb-2025 with only ~0.07% tendered, Burmans gained control and Saluja was voted off (97% against, Feb-2025). An allegation: a Nov-2023 Mumbai police FIR in the Mahadev betting-app case reportedly named Gaurav Burman (and reports said Mohit Burman); Dabur stated they had no connection -- unproven, no charge found in this scan. Investor read: a disciplined promoter at the flagship; takeovers have been by open offer at regulated prices (minorities could exit).

- **allegations:** Mahadev FIR naming (denied, unproven)
- **good conduct:** professional management; open offers at SEBI price

`person:group-ck-birla` · flag: **mostly-clean** · confidence: single-source · tickers: ORIENTELEC, HIL, BSOFT, ORIENTPPR

Flag: MOSTLY-CLEAN. Chandrakant Birla's group (an older branch of the Birla family). Listed: Orient Electric, HIL (Birla Aerocon, roofing), Birlasoft, Orient Paper & Industries, and formerly Orient Cement. Orient Cement sale (Oct-2024): Ambuja Cements (Adani) agreed to buy 46.8% at Rs 395.40/share (~Rs 8,100 cr, ~12% premium to prior close), triggering a mandatory 26% open offer to public shareholders at the same price; the letter of offer was delayed to May-2025 pending approvals -- minorities received the same price as promoters (good conduct). No regulator enforcement findings against the group were found in this scan; group companies are mid-caps with moderate leverage and no notable promoter pledges. Birlasoft has had CEO churn and the group has faced questions on sub-scale businesses (Orient Paper), but not on value transfers. Confidence: single-source for most items beyond the Orient Cement deal; verify SAST pledges and RPT notes before relying.

- **red flags:** none major found; sub-scale businesses
- **good conduct:** Orient Cement exit with open offer at same price

body:
**False alarm: Bharti Airtel's AGR losses, Rs 2 lakh cr debt and three equity raises** (`case_study:false-alarm-bharti-airtel-losses-debt`, verified). FLAGS: net loss Rs 30,664 cr (FY20) and Rs 12,364 cr (FY21) (Q2 FY20 alone -Rs 23,044 cr on a Rs 28,450 cr AGR provision); borrowings Rs 83,415 cr (FY15) -> Rs 2.26 lakh cr (FY23); ROCE 3-7% FY18-21; equity raised repeatedly: ~Rs 25,000 cr rights (May 2019, ~Rs 220/share), Rs 21,502 cr QIP+FCCB (Jan 2020), ~Rs 21,000 cr rights (2021). CONTEXT: the losses were a one-time court-ordered regulatory provision, not operating losses; CFO never went below Rs 18,000 cr and rose to Rs 1.22 lakh cr (FY26); working-capital days were deeply negative (-160 to -350); much of the debt is deferred spectrum payments to the government on long tenors; the Jio price war was consolidating the industry to three players, so tariffs would eventually rise. Governance graded clean (person:group-bharti) and promoters subscribed to rights. OPM went 32% (FY19) -> 55% (FY26). Stock: ~Rs 291 (2019) -> Rs 2,143 (Nov 2026), ~7.4x. LESSON: separate one-time provisions from operating results, and ask what kind of debt it is (government spectrum dues vs short-term bank loans). Equity raised to survive a consolidating price war, from a clean promoter who subscribes, is different from dilution to stay alive in a structurally losing market (Vodafone Idea).

**False alarm: APL Apollo's 5-8% operating margin** (`case_study:false-alarm-apl-apollo-low-margins`, verified). FLAG: OPM only 5-9% every year (FY19 5%, FY26 8%) in a steel-linked business; screens filtering on OPM > 15% exclude it. CONTEXT: return on capital, not margin, decides value. APL Apollo turned its capital very fast: working-capital days ~0 (dealers pay quickly; debtor days 3-6 since FY21), so ROCE was 20-32% at 5-8% margins. It also added differentiated products (Direct Forming Technology lines, 2016-17) and gained share (structural tubes ~40% per company). P/E was ~4-5 in 2013-14 because the market priced it as a commodity processor. Stock: Rs 3.22 (Mar 2009) -> Rs 2,148 (Nov 2026), ~670x. The same logic applies to DMart (8% OPM), Costco (~3% net margin) and Dixon (3-4% margin). WHEN LOW MARGIN IS A REAL FLAG: when asset turns are low too (ROCE < cost of capital), when the margin is shrinking because a rival has a cost advantage, or when tiny margins on huge revenue make the revenue itself hard to verify (Rajesh Exports at ~0.5%). LESSON: read margin x asset turn = ROCE; screen on ROCE and working-capital days, not OPM.

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:US-ADBE:cold-valuation-beats-spy-to-jun27`
- **Method:** valuation-temperature · **P(ours)** 0.52 · **P(base)** 0.48 · resolve by 2027-06-30
- **Evidence:** Yahoo monthly closes: ADBE $217.71 on 20-Nov-2026 (52-wk $190.12–362.71; all-time high ~$670); SPY $689.81. Q3 FY26 release (Sep-2026): record revenue $6.76bn (+13%), non-GAAP EPS $6.13, GAAP EPS $4.62, ARR $27.50bn, AI-first ARR +150%; FY26 revenue target raised to $26.576–26.626bn; Q4 target $6.80–6.85bn; CEO succession under way ('Anil' named as successor) and an interim CFO. ≈9× annualised non-GAAP EPS / ≈12× GAAP — very cold vs its own 10-year history (typically 25–45×, from memory).
- **Why our number differs from base:** Valuation-temperature test on a 'cold' quality name: double-digit growth at a single-digit-teens multiple is extreme for a software franchise, but the market is pricing AI disruption of creative tools, and cold-for-a-reason names often stay cold. Mean reversion is a weak 7-month force; we lean only slightly above the base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** A single US large cap beats SPY over ~7 months a bit under half the time (~48%; skewed single-stock returns).
- **Resolution rule:** YES if (ADBE close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 217.71) > (SPY close on 30-Jun-2027 ÷ 689.81). Use the last trading day ≤30-Jun-2027; adjust for splits; dividends ignored.
- **Resolution source:** Yahoo Finance / Nasdaq closes (ADBE, SPY)
- **Sources used:** https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/ADBE; https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/SPY; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/796343/000079634326000147/adbeex991q326.htm
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified
